method: Direct inspection of saved original PNG via view_image(detail=original), compared with supplied portrait, original frozen test-case and selected full source literal before receiving arm pixel verdict.

gates.evidence: The man alone grips the envelope. The woman holds an empty open palm with a clearly visible separation. The original criterion requires simultaneous two-owner contact on the same paper and is not met; the original criterion is retained.
Close public staging and divergent outward attention are clear. The original shared-contact handoff is instead a pre-contact offer; motive and secrecy cannot be inferred.
Flower buckets, wrapped bouquet, visible counter, commuter crowd and station departure board establish the intended public flower-stall/concourse setting.
Short dark bob, wispy bangs, dark eyes and soft face proportions follow the attached portrait broadly; no exact identity or age claim.

new_source_literal_review.mode: inspiration_only; exact complete English source sentence retained; native chosen lists empty
new_source_literal_review.literal: One person extends an envelope while the other person's open hand remains separated from it by a visible gap.

components.evidence: The cream envelope is held by the man’s fingers and his sleeve/forearm connects to the brown-coated body.
The woman’s open palm is empty and connects through the coat cuff and arm to her body.
The envelope edge is distinctly above and apart from the woman’s palm and fingertips in the same view.

new_source_literal_review.limits: This supports the one complete selected visible realization. It is not formal whole-native source adoption/approval or qualification of the other 110 new visual candidates.

artistic_observation: The adjacent bodies and separated gazes create a clear tense public encounter. Bouquet and station context connect well; a visible offered envelope gives the frame a specific moment. Intent, allegiance, envelope content and a future completed exchange remain unobservable.
crosscheck_after_arm_review: The arm also identified that the man’s eyes and upper head are outside the crop. Root confirms this in the original: head orientation is readable, but precise eye-line toward the departure board is not.
